title: Om pendant: meaning and how to wear it
description: What Om means in Hindu tradition, how the symbol is commonly read, and practical tips on wearing an Om pendant the right way up, with the right chain.
intro: Om is considered the most sacred sound in Hindu tradition, a single syllable that is chanted at the start of prayers and mantras and is seen as representing the whole of existence. An Om pendant is worn as a quiet reminder of that, and also simply as a symbol of faith. Wearing one is easy, but there are a few customs worth knowing, from which way the symbol should face to what it pairs well with.

sections.heading: What Om stands for
paragraphs: Om, also written Aum, appears in the Vedas and the Upanishads and is chanted before most mantras, from the Gayatri Mantra to Om Namah Shivaya. The Mandukya Upanishad is the text most often quoted about it. It explains Om as three sounds, A, U and M, followed by silence. These are traditionally linked with the waking state, the dreaming state, deep sleep, and a fourth state beyond all three.

Because of this, Om is not tied to one deity. It is used in the worship of Shiva, Vishnu, the Goddess and Ganesha alike, which makes an Om pendant one of the most widely accepted devotional pieces you can wear or gift within Hindu families.

sections.heading: Reading the written symbol
paragraphs: The Devanagari Om has a shape most of us know by heart, but not everyone knows the popular way it is explained. This explanation is a later one rather than something spelled out in the Upanishad itself, and you will find small differences depending on who tells it.
Still, it is a handy way to remember what the sound is meant to point towards each time you glance at your pendant. The commonly shared version goes like this:
list: The large lower curve: the waking state, when we experience the world through the senses.
The middle curve: the dreaming state.
The upper curve: deep, dreamless sleep.
The crescent above: maya, the illusion that separates us from the highest state.
The dot at the top: that highest state, often called turiya.

sections.heading: Om in other traditions
paragraphs: Om is sacred in Jainism and Buddhism as well, and it opens many Buddhist mantras, including Om Mani Padme Hum. The Sikh symbol Ik Onkar is a different symbol with its own meaning in Sikh teaching, so it is best not to treat the two as interchangeable when gifting. If you are buying for a friend from another faith, ask which symbol they would actually like to wear.

sections.heading: How to wear an Om pendant
paragraphs: There are no strict scriptural rules for wearing an Om pendant, but these customs are followed in many homes:
list: Make sure it hangs the right way up, with the dot and crescent at the top. A pendant that flips easily is worth fixing with a better bail.
Let it sit close to the heart or the base of the throat. A chain of roughly 18 to 22 inches works for most people.
Many people avoid wearing Om as an anklet, toe ring or on a waist chain, since sacred symbols are traditionally kept above the waist.
Some take it off before visiting a cremation ground or during mourning, as they would with other religious jewellery. Practices vary by family.
Put it on after a bath, perhaps with a short chant of Om, if you would like the first wear to feel special.

sections.heading: Picking the right style
paragraphs: An Om pendant comes in many forms, and each suits a different person and setting. A plain Om in 925 silver is subtle enough for school, college or office, and works for both men and women. Silver with a small CZ outline adds sparkle for festive days. You can find these in the [silver pendant collection](/silver).

If you would like the Om to sit alongside rudraksha, a chain mala with an Om pendant brings the two most common Shaiva symbols together in one piece. The [Om rudraksha chain malas at Varaha](/divine) have gold-plated pendants on a bead chain and are made for wearing over a kurta or a plain tee. Larger pendants look best on longer chains; smaller ones on shorter chains, so they do not get lost in the neckline.

sections.heading: Keeping it looking good
paragraphs: Silver Om pendants tarnish over time; a silver polishing cloth used once a week or so keeps them bright, and storing them in an airtight pouch slows the darkening. Gold-plated pendants should be kept away from water, perfume and sweat, and wiped with a dry cloth after wearing. Never use toothpaste or lemon on plated pieces, as both rub the colour off.

faq.q: Can anyone wear an Om pendant?
faq.a: Yes. Om is not tied to one deity, so it is widely worn by people of all ages and genders across Hindu, Jain and Buddhist traditions.

faq.q: Which metal is best for an Om pendant?
faq.a: That depends on use. 925 silver suits daily wear; gold-plated pieces look festive but need more care around water and perfume.

faq.q: Is it disrespectful to wear Om as fashion?
faq.a: Most people see no problem as long as it is worn with respect: the right way up, kept clean, and not worn on the feet.
